# Every frame names the message that opened it

A frame carries its triggering message id, the message type, the sender and the
sender kind. An operator asking why a frame opened is answered directly, without
correlating an external system's logs with the instance.

## The deployment

A webhook publisher paired with the deployment:

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers: {}
named_locks: {}
executors: {}
publishers:
  "hook":
    endpoint: "webhook-sensor:9084"
    protocols: ["publisher"]
```

## A template that produces all three origins

```yaml
name: frame-origin-demo
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: loop/iterate
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        value: {type: integer}
      required: [value]
  - type: hook/in
  - type: ops/kick
publishers:
  - name: hook
    kind: webhook
    message_type: hook/in
    config:
      path_prefix: /inbound
      auth:
        mode: secret_header
        header: X-Token
        secret: "<your secret>"
nodes:
  - type: counter
    kind: loop_counter
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/kick
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 9}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: sender
    sends_message: loop/iterate
    subscribes:
      - node: counter
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: counter
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          value: {type: integer, source: "{{nodes.counter.attribute.count}}"}
        required: [value]

  - type: receiver
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: loop/iterate
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          got: {type: integer, source: "{{messages.loop/iterate.value}}"}

  - type: hooked
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: hook/in
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          v: {type: integer, default: 1}
```

## Drive all three origins

An operator message:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"type":"ops/kick"}'
```

A publisher message — POST to the webhook sensor:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:$HOOK_PORT/inbound" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "X-Token: <your secret>" \
  -d '{"event":"poke"}'
```

A message the instance sends itself: the `sender` node above sends
`loop/iterate` when the counter settles.

## Read the frames

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/frames"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/frames/$FRAME_ID"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/messages/$TRIGGERING_MESSAGE_ID"
```

Three frames come back. Each names a `triggering_message_id`, a `message_type`,
a `message_sender` and a `message_sender_kind`. The three sender kinds are
`operator`, `publisher` and `instance`.

Reading one frame on its own returns the same trigger the list gave. Each
triggering message id resolves through the messages route to a message whose
type and sender kind match what the frame reported: the two records agree.

Narrowing the frame list by a triggering message id returns that one frame.

## One naming note

A message the instance itself sent is reported with sender kind `instance` and
sender `instance:<id>` — the sending instance's own id — rather than being
labelled a cascade-sent message.
